title: Infant of a Diabetic Mother
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Infant of Diabetic Mother
Adamkin DH; AAP Committee on Fetus and Newborn. Pediatrics 2011;127(3):575-579
Thornton PS et al; Pediatric Endocrine Society. J Pediatr 2015;167(2):238-245

changelog.change: Initial entry — the hyperinsulinemia mechanism, the complications by system, the two competing glucose thresholds (AAP vs PES), and the treatment of symptomatic hypoglycemia / hypocalcemia / polycythemia.

purpose: Maternal hyperglycemia → fetal hyperinsulinemia → macrosomia + delayed lung maturation, and after birth the hallmark risk: neonatal hypoglycemia. Feed early, screen glucose, and know which threshold your unit uses.

body.text: Maternal hyperglycemia crosses the placenta → fetal hyperglycemia → pancreatic β-cell hyperplasia and hyperinsulinemia → fat / glycogen deposition (macrosomia), organomegaly, delayed surfactant maturation. At birth the maternal glucose supply stops while fetal insulin is still transiently high → hypoglycemia.

rows: Macrosomia (most common) OR SGA if maternal vasculopathy limited placental flow
RDS (hyperinsulinemia delays surfactant), perinatal asphyxia, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (usually transient, septal-predominant)
Polycythemia (relative fetal hypoxia drives EPO), hyperbilirubinemia
Risk tied to first-trimester glycemic control (HbA1c) — cardiac (VSD, transposition), neural tube defects, caudal regression, renal

body.text: Glucose thresholds — two guidelines, different purposes

rows: First 24–48 h, at-risk infants (IDM, SGA/LGA, late preterm)
Persistent / recurrent hypoglycemia beyond 48 h — evaluate for an underlying disorder

body.text: Symptoms of neonatal hypoglycemia: jitteriness, irritability, high-pitched cry; lethargy, hypotonia, poor feeding; apnea, cyanosis; seizures (severe / prolonged).

rows: D10W 2 mL/kg IV bolus, then a continuous infusion at a glucose infusion rate (GIR) of 6–8 mg/kg/min; recheck and titrate
Trial oral feeding first if feasible, recheck within ~1 h; if still low or symptomatic, treat as above
10% calcium gluconate 1–2 mL/kg (100–200 mg/kg) IV slowly over 10 min with cardiac monitoring; may repeat
Monitor hematocrit; partial exchange transfusion if symptomatic and Hct markedly elevated

body.text: GIR (mg/kg/min) = (IV rate mL/hr × dextrose % × 0.167) ÷ weight kg. Start at 6–8; escalate the concentration (needs central access above ~12.5%) or rate if glucose stays low — persistent need for GIR > 8–10 raises concern for hyperinsulinism.

buildNote: Tier 1. A GIR calculator is a natural companion (formula engine). Antenatal glycemic control (target HbA1c) is the upstream prevention.  Related: nrp-algorithm, neonatal-seizures, neonatal-jaundice, perioperative-glycemic-management.
